items.text: [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/26623866/aa2449adc6815e9807ba9d663ed53ca21f1ae81a.png"]Greetings, Warriors of Calradia!
War Sails v1.3.7 and Bannerlord v1.5.7 are now live on PC, with the console release planned once the release process for them concludes.
Join us in watching the video below as we walk through the key highlights included in this update. Prefer reading instead? You can find the full text breakdown further below.
Owning a fleet has always demanded substantial progress - ships of your own, and crews that man them. We wanted to keep that intact while opening up more ways to access naval content earlier.
The first is the ability to begin your Sandbox with a small trading ship through the new Advanced Starting Options. We’ll talk about those in a minute.

Next, we have the ferry. You can now travel between certain coastal villages without owning a single ship. You'll need to be in a coastal village, out of an army, with less than fifty troops, and carrying the fare, which scales with your party size and the hostility of both ends of the trip.
And for when you're just starting out, we've made the waters a little more approachable as well. Smaller pirate parties now spawn to give new captains encounters they can successfully take on.

Then, as you move on to building up a fleet, you have more flexibility in deciding which ships to take with you. You can now moor ships rather than selling them or sending them to your clan, and sail out only with the fleet that suits what you're doing - be that trading, raiding, or a straight fight.
Finally, we've added port points to coastal castles and extended the siege blockade feature to them, which should provide more opportunities for fleets to clash at sea.
Of course, not every event at sea needs to end in a battle that requires a strong fleet to enjoy it.
We've taken the random-event system already familiar from land gameplay and brought it to naval interactions, with 39 new events for you to discover on the water.
Each one tells its own short story and puts a choice in front of you - and those choices can affect your character's traits, skills, party, items, or gold.
And for when a naval encounter does turn into a fight, we’ve made boarding more interactive too. It now has a counter.
Attachment ropes can be hit and destroyed by the player, denying the enemy their bridge before it ever forms. Rope physics have been overhauled as well, and behave more realistically.
So that covers some of the ways we expanded the early naval experience. But War Sails isn’t the only place where we’ve added more choice at the start of the game.
The same idea extends to Bannerlord through Advanced Starting options - a set of choices made when you begin a Sandbox campaign, split into three categories.

Campaign Scenarios shape the world itself. Imagine starting with a United Empire, a faction holding most of the map, a kingdom on the brink of destruction, two factions left standing, a more or less randomized Calradia, and with War Sails, Nords that have expanded south beyond their former borders.

Player Starts shape your own position instead. Begin as a King, a Vassal, a Mercenary clan under contract, an established Trader, an Outlaw wanted across Calradia, or a Beggar with nothing but rags. In War Sails, you can start as a vassal with a fleet, or a merchant with trade ships and a convoy.
Then there are Modifiers, which can be stacked on top of any combination. Inflate bandit parties, raise rebellion chances, reduce recruits generation, and increase travel speed on land and sea.

Put those three categories together, and you can create some very different starting conditions. Every campaign uses a seed to randomize its details, which you can share with a friend to recreate the same Calradia.
And Fast Mode now lives inside ASO rather than as a separate module - which is also how we brought it to consoles.

Once you’ve chosen how your Sandbox begins, you will now come across Battle Sites and Wreckages. They appear on the campaign map where battles took place, and can be investigated by you - or by the looters and pirates that are drawn to them.

Bigger sites take more time and troops to search, but the rewards scale with them. You might turn up with wounded survivors to recruit, along with denars, trade goods, and scavenged valuables that grant Roguery experience, or a map to a nearby bandit hideout. Your Roguery skill and party size determine how quickly you search.
Moving to traits - they have always influenced AI behaviour, but their impact was difficult to see. Each personality trait now carries effects - usually two positive and one negative.
For example, Merciful and Compassionate characters capture more prisoners instead of killing them, increase village hearth growth rate, but receive less gold when ransoming captured lords and troops.
On the flip side of the Mercy coin, Cruel and Sadistic characters gain more loot from raiding, decrease rebellion chance, but kill more prisoners instead of capturing them in battle.
Every trait works this way, across Calculating, Generosity, Honor, Mercy and Valor, and AI lords benefit from theirs as well.

Executions now also reach further than a relation hit. Executing a member of another clan can start a blood feud - and it cuts both ways, as an AI clan can start one with you when relations are low enough.

Once a feud is running, your clan members toss a coin on whether to execute captured rivals. The AI doesn't - given the chance, they will always execute you and your kin. Each day a captor holds one of your clan members, execution becomes more likely.
Fortunately, feuds don't have to last forever. They can be settled through Ransom Brokers or if relations climb back to zero.

We've also added finer control over clan party behavior, no longer relying on broader party stances. Those have been replaced by direct toggles. Rather than influencing a behaviour score, you can now directly allow or prohibit raiding villages, donating troops to garrisons, joining other armies, and - in War Sails - owning a fleet.
On the content side, four new battle terrains have been added to the following locations: 2 south of Ortysia, one southeast of Quyaz, and one south of Baltakhand.
For our multiplayer community, Captain Mode gains formation targeting with captains now having the ability to issue targeted charge orders to infantry, ranged, and cavalry formations alike.
This version also brings the Streamer mode which adds new displays, camera controls, and other tweaks while spectating.
That covers the highlights for War Sails v1.3.7 and Bannerlord v1.5.7. Here’s an image to recap the important changes as well.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/26623866/f704e7167a73908fd2d3ea941aaf531ef701c4ce.png"]
The following changes are specific to the War Sails expansion and are not part of the base game.
Settlement Actions (Town, Village, Castle and Hideout)
Added Mooring to Town Ports

In neutral or allied towns, you can now moor your ships and configure your fleet composition without selling or sending to clan. You can moor at multiple ports without a ship limit. Your existing moored ports will become inaccessible if the town owner is at war with you, and become accessible again once they are no longer hostile.
Added a ferry system that enables you to travel between some coastal villages without owning ships

To use a ferry, you must be in a coastal village (including the hostile ones), not be in an army, have a party size of no more than 50 troops, and carry enough gold to cover the fare. The fare depends on your party size and the hostility of both the departure and destination settlements, with the hostile village ferry charging more. The destination is preset for each coastal village and is visible in the village menu.
Added the ability to embark and disembark at coastal castles, and extended the siege blockade feature to coastal castles as well.
Fixed a bug that caused the lost battle simulation of Seaborne Village Raid to be considered as a win if the simulation is started right after losing the Seaborne Village Raid mission battle.
Fixed a bug that caused position errors of the player's party after setting sail, preventing the party from entering settlements.
Random Events
Added 39 naval random events. These appear based on your actions at sea. Each event tells a different story and offers choices that can affect your character’s traits, skills, party, items, or gold.
Character Development System
Changed how you gain the Boatswain skill experience. It is no longer gained when your ships take damage. Instead, you can develop the Boatswain skill by maintaining high party morale while at sea.
Increased the amount of Boatswain experience gained from repairing ships.
Added missing naval skills (Mariner, Boatswain, Shipmaster) to faction leader skill templates.
Reduced most non-governor perks' effects by 50% when used in naval battles (perks that are not in the Mariner, Boatswain, or Shipmaster category and those that adjust numeric values).
Made Boatswain - Streamlined Operations, Shipwrights Insight, Smooth Operator, and Accuracy Training perks' FirstMate role effects Captain effects.
Made Boatswain - Shipwrights Insight's primary effect a personal effect, which now only applies when the hero who has the perk uses a ballista on a ship.
Nord nobles now have beards and facial scars more often to make them appear more rugged.
Fixed a bug that prevented the Mariner - Forceful perk from applying its secondary effect properly.
Campaign Map
Improved terrain features and visuals of the world map.
Reduced visible grid lines on the world map.
Switched a terrain scene near Makeb with a more suitable one.
Fixed a bug that prevented parts of the world map from applying the correct weather based on the campaign time, leading to campaign map and mission scenes having inconsistent weather.
Fixed a bug that caused incorrect pathfinding on the campaign map.
Fixed a bug that caused battle missions to trigger a scene with a winter setting when started under the storm on the campaign map.
Naval Battles
Ship attachment ropes can now be hit by the player and destroyed to prevent bridges from being formed.
Additionally, attachment rope physics have been overhauled and made more realistic.

Relaxed the skeletal crew restriction for ship placement during the OoB phase. You can now deploy ships that have fewer troops than the skeletal crew number. The UI will alert you that such ships will underperform in battle.

Improved deployment zone planning for naval battles. Ship spacing is now dynamically adjusted based on deployment width, with a maximum gap of 20 meters that scales down for wider formations in river battles (e.g., 13 meters for 8 dromons). River battles now use a fixed deployment zone depth with 50-meter front and back margins, while sea battles continue to extend the zone toward mission boundaries.
Fixed a bug that caused ship collisions to have numerous camera shakes or deal damage more than once.
Fixed a bug that caused retreated ships to be displayed as destroyed in the mission scoreboard.
Fixed a bug that prevented ships from being displayed in the scoreboard during a custom battle seaborne village raid.
Fixed a bug that prevented troops from boarding the enemy ship in some scenarios.
Fixed a bug that allowed players to place troop formations in unintended areas during Seaborne and Village raid missions in OoB.
Fixed a bug that allowed the naval battle to start even with undermanned ships deployed.
Fixed a bug that prevented crew members from taking control of the ship when delegating command of the vessel.
Clan and Party

Improved AI noble party decision-making when encountering pirates at sea. Parties now consider their active task and proximity to friendly or enemy settlements before deciding whether to engage, reducing unnecessary interruptions and helping them stay focused on their current objectives. Parties traveling by sea near enemy settlements or parties performing Offensive Patrol tasks will now no longer engage pirate parties unless those pirates are already engaged with a friendly (own faction, alliance, or trade agreement) party.
Added smaller pirate parties to increase early game accessibility of naval encounters.
Fixed a bug that allowed the player to set sail from hostile villages.
Fixed a bug that caused naval patrols to have trouble navigating curved rivers.
Fixed a bug that caused nobles to be embarking to their ships for 30+ hours, during which they couldn't be interacted with.
Fixed a bug that caused parties without a ship to try defending a raided village from the water.
Ships & Upgrades
Improved the descriptions of ship upgrades.
Added a new animation pose to the captain point of the Ghurab ship.
Fixed a bug that prevented the "Reinforced Battlements with Improved Rudder" ship upgrade from appearing visually.
Fixed a bug that prevented the top two parts of cloth on the Square Sails (level 3) from being affected by wind physics.
Fixed a bug that prevented colors from showing on ship sails and rooftops.
Fixed a bug that caused different LODs to change ship roof color.
UI
Changed the mariner icon visibility check when upgrading troops. It no longer looks at whether the current mariner is a mariner, but whether the upgraded version of the troop is a mariner.
Improved the ordering of scoreboard ships to show the player's ships first, in their formation orders (1->8).
Updated draft type in the Fleet Menu to include naval raid ability.
Updated some ship thumbnails.
Removed the + ship buttons from custom battle Seaborne Village Raids beyond the 3 ships.
Fixed a bug that allowed you to open other screens while the Manage Fleet screen was open.
Quests & Issues
Made a pass over the early and mid War Sails storyline to reduce difficulty in certain missions:
Adjusted enemy weapons in the alley fight and the ship escape to deal less damage.
Increased the duration of Gunnar's invulnerability after he is rescued following the in-mission cinematic of the alley fight.
Increased the allied ship's troop count to 14 in Escort the Vlandian Merchants.
Increased the fireship's health in Break Out of Omor Estuary so that it is much harder to sink before reaching the target ship.
Increased the second ship's maximum health and maximum fire health in Break Out of Omor Estuary.
Added an Alt-key highlight to the throwable axe barrels on the escape ship in Free the Sea Hounds' Captives, making them easier to find during the escape phase.
Updated the equipment and skills of the Vlandian Merchant, Sea Hound Recruit, and Sea Hound Thug troops.
Fixed a bug that prevented the first enemy ship from firing its ballista in Break Out of Omor Estuary.
Added postures and animations to characters in the naval storyline dialogues.
Fixed a bug that caused enemy troops to spawn inside water during the Army of Poachers quest in some villages.
Fixed a bug that prevented the player from correctly starting at the ship helm when choosing to control the captured ship during the Defeat the Sea Hounds mission.
Audio
Fixed a bug that caused Sturgian Victory music to be played instead of Nord when winning an encounter.
Fixed a bug that caused the Battle music to disappear during the finale of the Naval Storyline missions.
Fixed a bug that caused all naval battles to end with the Battanian Victory music. They now end with your faction's Victory music or the music of the troops' dominant culture.
Animations
Fixed a bug that caused banner animation issues during the Seaborne Village Raid on the world map.
Other
Made 14 armour pieces appear in Nord town shops instead of Sturgia.
Updated Skolderbrotva troops and their leaders with Nord culture items.
Updated Sea Raider troops' equipment with Nord culture items.
Fixed a bug that allowed some Nord female dresses to be equipped by male characters.
Crashes
Fixed a crash that occurred when entering a Scourge of the Seas quest due to other unrelated quests. They're now cancelled.
Fixed a crash that occurred when the player lost the battle in Seaborne Village Raid mission but won it in the battle simulation afterwards.
Fixed a crash that occurred when the player used cheats to kill their character during War Sails storyline missions.
The following changes are part of the base game and apply to the War Sails expansion as well.
Advanced Starting Options (ASO)
Campaign Scenarios - Choose a starting scenario to shape Calradia. ASO uses it as a guideline, randomizes the campaign state, and lets you share the result through the Seed system.
Default: Calradia as you know it.
United Empire: The civil war has ended, and your chosen imperial faction has reunited the Calradian Empire.
Invasion: Faction of your choosing expanded aggressively and is now ruling most of Calradia.
Last Stand: Faction of your choosing is on the brink of destruction and has a single town left, where they will make their last stand.
2 Faction War: Every faction but the two factions of your choosing has been eliminated, Calradia is divided into two and is at war.
Randomized Calradia: Randomizes the starting state of Calradia to the degree of your choosing.
\ Nord Invasion: The Nords have arrived to Calradia and started an aggressive campaign. They have expanded south and are looking for more.

Player Starts - Choose a player start to shape your journey. Each start works with any Campaign Scenario and is randomized through the Seed system. Some player starts must be unlocked: reach King, Vassal, or Mercenary rank, or create your first caravan to unlock Trader. Loading existing saves with fulfilled conditions also unlocks the relevant starts.
Default: Default sandbox player start.
King: Your character starts as a Ruler of a faction of your choice.
Vassal: Start as a vassal of a faction of your choice.
Mercenary: Start as a small clan in mercenary service of a faction of your choice.
Trader: Start as a trader with a workshop and a caravan to your name in a random town.
Outlaw: Start as an outlaw that’s wanted by all the factions in Calradia.
Beggar: Start with nothing but the ragged clothes on your back.
\ Fleet Admiral: Start as a vassal of a faction of your choice, with a force at sea.
\ Merchant Venturer: Start as a merchant venturer on sea with trade ships, a set up convoy and a workshop in a random town.
Modifiers - Apply multiple modifiers alongside any Campaign Scenario and Player Start.
Bandit Surge: Increases bandit party sizes globally, with huge ones occasionally.
Civil Unrest: Increases rebellion chances globally.
Recruit Shortage: Decreases the recruit generation of notables significantly.
Swift Travel: Increases the travel speed globally on both land and sea.
\ Personal Vessel: Start with a small trading ship to your name.

Seed system - Seeds randomize campaign generation, player-start details, and other sandbox elements. You can share your seed and ASO options with a friend to recreate the same sandbox, or just your seed for partial parity.
Fast Mode has been moved to ASO, is no longer a separate Module, and is intended to become available on Consoles through this as well.
Battle Sites & Wreckages

After battles on land or sea, battle sites and wreckages can now appear on the campaign map, marking where the fight took place. These can be investigated for loot, survivors, or other findings by you or looter and pirate parties, which are drawn to them.
Battle Sites & Wreckages come in three sizes. Larger ones require more time and troops to investigate, but offer greater potential rewards.
Small battles can leave Skirmish Sites and Wreckages.
Medium battles can leave Battlegrounds and Battle Wreckages.
Large battles can leave Battle Aftermaths which are named after the nearest settlement.
Investigating a Battle Site / Wreckage may yield all of the following which scale with the site size:

Wounded surviving troops that can be recruited into your party. The number of troops recovered also depends on the highest Medicine skill among your party’s heroes, and grants Medicine XP to that hero.
Denars.
Trade goods & scavenged valuables. The former also provide Roguery XP when looted.
A map revealing a nearby bandit hideout.
How fast you search a site is also impacted by your Roguery skill and party size.
Battle Sites and Wreckages eventually disappear, with Aftermaths being converted into Battle Remains - sticking around on the campaign map for longer even after being investigated.
Character Development System
New Effects for Personality Traits
Each now usually provides two positive and one negative effects.
Calculating
Calculating → Cerebral
+10% / +20% Workshop income
+10% / +20% Siege engine construction speed
Starting relation with notables you meet for the first time: −3 / −6
Impulsive → Hotheaded (negative side)
+5% / +10% Charge damage for troops under your command
+10% / +20% Combat starting morale
Disorganized state after losing a fight lasts +50% / +100% longer
Generosity
Generous → Munificent
+25% / +50% additional mercenaries
+10% / +20% Party morale gain rate
+10% Food consumption
Closefisted → Tightfisted (negative side)
+10% / +20% Town project effectiveness
−5% / −10% Troop wages
−1 party morale per day (both tiers)
Honor
Honest → Honorable
+10% / +20% Relationship gain rate
+10% / +20% Settlement loyalty gain rate
Crime rating decays 40% / 80% slower
Devious → Deceitful (negative side)
Crime rating rises 40% / 80% slower when you commit crimes
Recruiting bandits/prisoners costs 15% / 25% less morale penalty
+5% / +10% Amplified relation swings (gains AND losses) with clan leaders
Mercy
Merciful → Compassionate
+25% / +50% Chance to capture prisoners instead of killing them
+5% / +10% Village hearth growth rate
0% / −20% Gold when ransoming captured lords
−20% / 0% Gold when ransoming captured troops
Cruel → Sadistic (negative side)
+20% / +40% Raid loot yield
−20% / −40% Rebellion chance
−25% / −50% Chance to capture prisoners (you kill more instead)
Valor
Daring → Fearless
+10% / +20% Resistance to morale loss from battle losses
+10% / +20% Renown gained after battles
−5% / −10% HP recovery per day
Cautious → Very Cautious (negative side)
−10% / −20% Personnel casualties during siege simulations
−25% / −50% Prisoners under your command/governorship escape less often
Siege preparation takes 30% / 60% longer
Hovering over characters in the encyclopedia now shows a tooltip showing their traits and effects.
Added trait change information to the tooltips of siege aftermath options.

Rebalanced the personality traits of rogue/bandit-type wanderers. Most lost Mercy and Generosity, being replaced with Calculating, Honor, and Valor. Cowardly/bandit characters are now Cautious, and dishonorable wanderers are Devious.
Your character now also gains Leadership experience while maintaining high morale.
Nobles, player companions, and wanderers now gain XP daily based on their focus points.
Reintroduced the "Character Leveled Up" indicator to the character development screen.
Stealth items are now also passed to the heir upon main character's death.
Made children visually resemble their parents even more by reducing static body-property randomization.
Fixed a bug that caused Auto Allocate Clan Member Perks to select the perks even when the option is off.

Fixed a bug that prevented dismount, knockdown, and knockback-related combat perks (ShowOfStrength, HardKnock, KeepAtBay, Skewer, Braced, HammerBolts, KnockOff) from applying their perk effect correctly.
Blood Feuds
Blood Feuds make executions more consequential. You can start a feud with a clan by executing one of their members.
Executing a noble already affects your Honor and Mercy traits, as well as relations with their clan, faction, and friendly clans. Executing dishonorable nobles carries fewer negative consequences.
AI clans can also start a Blood Feud by executing one of your clan members. This may occur when relations are low (at least -50), and is influenced by the captor’s Mercy trait.
Your clan members toss a coin on whether to execute captured members of the rival clan when given the opportunity.
The AI clan member will always choose to execute the player if given the opportunity.

Each day, AI captors become increasingly likely to execute your clan members, reaching a guaranteed chance on day 10. If they enter a settlement, they instead hand over the prisoner for execution 8 days later.
No ransom offers between the feuding clans are allowed.

Blood Feuds can be settled through Ransom Brokers. Only executed family members are counted: if you lost or tied the feud, it ends only for a small commission; if you executed more, you must pay compensation. Relations between both clans are then set to -50.
Blood Feuds also end if the relations between the feuding clans reach 0.
Blood Feuds block the following with the rival clan: defections, faction membership and invitations if they come from a ruling clan, as well as safe-passage agreements.
Clan and Party
Clan Party Controls
Replaced party stances with behavior toggles.
Party stances did not have a reliable, recognizable gameplay impact outside of preventing raids in the defensive stance.

notes.title: The new behavioral toggles can enable/disable

items.text: Raiding villages
Donating troops to garrisons
Joining other armies
\ Owning a naval fleet
Added the clan party recovery system, which holds the party slot for defeated clan parties and spawns the party with the same configuration from a safe location.
\ Additionally, if the clan party is defeated on land, their ships will be returned to them upon respawning.
Removed the finance screen from the Clan tab.
\\ Increased the naval and land party speeds by 15%.
Improved positioning of world map party visuals during battles by placing them closer to the center of the battle in an arc formation.
Fixed a bug that prevented the automatic addition of troops to companions that were promoted to vassals.
Fixed a bug that caused the changing party leader UI to open the clan screen without displaying the party leader change prompt.
Art
Added 4 new battle terrains to locations in the image.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/26623866/4103f51fdd27a58347ae8ee154f55bfee16598b6.png"]
Added the corresponding Seaborne Village Raid scenes to Land Custom Battle.
Improved rendering performance of the main menu videos.
Fixed some collision issues with walls in Omor.
Fixed a bug that prevented Dagby, Ykerslund, and Amycon's village scenes from triggering correct mission scenes.
Fixed a bug that prevented the intended starting stealth equipment from appearing in the inventory.
Battles and Sieges
Reinforcement Deployment

Improved reinforcement deployment positions. Reinforcements spawn on one of the invisible scene paths, with the initial path determined by the parties' world map positions. The reinforcement path selection algorithm avoids spawning units too close to enemies. It now prioritizes the two neighboring paths that are radially closest to the initial path. This keeps reinforcements closer to their expected approach direction and prevents cases where they arrive from a wildly different side of the scene.
Fixed a bug that caused reinforcements to arrive near the middle of the reinforcement path, instead of near the beginning or the end of the path.
Caravan Equipment Deployment Improvements

Fixed a bug in caravan encounters that caused caravan equipment to be placed on an incorrect position. It is now placed at the very end of the path, close to the initial spawn area of the caravan troops.

Even though caravan equipment may now spawn at mission start, its associated tactical position is added after OOB deployment is completed, and the TeamAI tactic of the caravan team is reset. This prevents the troops assigned to protect the caravan from teleporting during OOB deployment and overlapping with the caravan. Instead, they spawn in front of the caravan and then move to protect it.
Reduced the friendly bump attacks made by troops in a shield wall by improving combat collisions.

Improved the troop placement in the column arrangement. Units now try to form a column first before following the unit in front of them. This should prevent a bug that caused some agents to get stuck in the column.
Improved the aiming of AI troops while using the ballista.

Fixed a bug that caused AI agents holding position to ignore a lone attacker harassing them. They can now break off in small squads to pursue and counter-attack the attacker, whether it's the player or a stray enemy, until the attacker is dealt with or retreats back toward their allies.
Fixed a bug that caused an automatic win when sallying out after a successful ambush battle in siege.
Fixed a bug that prevented bastard swords from being used as two-handers.
Fixed a bug that prevented troop positions from being restored when the Reset Deployment button was used in the Order of Battle screen.
Fixed a bug that caused troops with raised shields to turn their backs to incoming ranged attacks.
Fixed a bug that prevented ranged units with an Engage order from attacking due to continuous back-and-forth movement.
Fixed a bug that caused mangonels and trebuchets to consistently miss their targets under certain configurations.
UI
Added a new popup that shows hero portraits and information in a larger and more detailed manner when selecting Party Roles.
Adjusted the Stealth Tutorial conversation text and trigger conditions so that it is clearer that the mission can be started only during the night.
Newly unlocked crafting pieces now stay highlighted until hovering across them with a mouse instead of requiring just the closure of the crafting screen.
Changed the army's food tooltip to bring it closer to the party's food tooltip. Also added the daily food change.
Changed the default tab behaviour in Clan and Kingdom screens. Opening those screens now shows the tabs that were accessed last.
The max party size is now shown to the player when choosing a party leader for a new or existing clan party.
Added a tooltip to the "Resolve Decision" button in the Fiefs tab to inform the player that they can't interact with it during a siege.
Added D-Pad navigation to the search bar in the inventory screen.
Separated the kingdom and clan leader filters in the Encyclopedia Heroes page.
Tweaked the encyclopedia filters for clans and kingdoms.
Removed the text "Distance to army" shown in an army member's pop up once they joined the army.
Fixed a bug that caused locked sliders in custom battle to visually remain at zero after finishing a battle.
Fixed a formatting bug with tribute texts in the Kingdom tab.
Fixed a bug that caused siege engine icons to appear in front of the OoB deployment layer.
Fixed a bug that prevented the game menu from appearing after returning to the world map from a siege.
Fixed a text bug with the "Confirm" button in the barter screen.
Fixed a bug that caused the same alley name to be displayed twice inside the tooltip of notables in a settlement.
Fixed a bug that caused the formation icon to continuously jump between last two remaining troops in the formation.
Fixed a bug that prevented "None" (default) crafting pieces from being correctly placed at the beginning of the pieces grid.
Fixed a bug that caused the prisoner to be released when selecting the "Forget It" option in the execution prompt.
Kingdoms and Diplomacy

Fixed a bug in relation to consequences of hostile actions against villages. Previously, any hostile action carried a risk of starting a war. Now, war is triggered only if the village resists and the player chooses to attack. If the village does not resist, the action increases only the player’s crime rating.
Fixed a bug that allowed kingdoms to persist without any fiefs when a non-leader clan owned all the fiefs and defected from the kingdom.
Fixed a bug that allowed a party to join an encounter where both sides were enemies, which caused a never-ending war.
Settlement Actions (Town, Village, Castle and Hideout)
Removed the loyalty penalty for assigning a governor whose culture differs from the settlement’s culture.
Fixed a bug that caused your character to "die in battle" while waiting in a town.
Fixed a bug that caused your companions to behave as village workers when visiting villages.
Fixed a bug that prevented the auto recruitment in towns from working correctly.
Fixed a bug that caused the tavern keeper to suggest the same companion for different skill types repeatedly.
Fixed a bug that caused an agent to stand near the main hero if their target point was occupied by the main hero, for example, a throne.
Quests & Issues
Radagos and Galter are now only visible in the Encyclopedia during their related quests.
Conspiracy parties created by the main storyline conspiracy quests are now shown as part of a conspiracy clan instead of bandit factions.
Fixed a bug that prevented the target hideout from being revealed to the player during the Conspiracy Base of Operations quest.
Fixed a bug that caused another conspiracy quest to start right after finishing one.

Fixed a bug that prevented the gold looting of raider parties in quests: Escort Merchant Caravan, Set Sail and Escort The Fortune Seekers, Destroy Raiders, Caravan Ambush, Extortion by Deserters, Company of Trouble.
Fixed a bug that caused low frequency of the Escort Merchant Caravan quest.
Fixed a bug that gave the "Long live the Empire!" achievement once the "Defeat the conspiracy" quest was cancelled or failed.
Fixed a bug that prevented quest giver notables' power from decreasing upon failing Need Manual Laborers, Army of Poachers, Village Needs Draught and Notable Wants Daughter Found quests.
Fixed a bug that caused Village Needs Draught Animals quest to fail instead of cancel if the village hearth is not within the correct range.
Fixed a bug that caused the Army of Poachers quest to fail instead of cancel when the village is raided by an AI party.
Fixed a bug that prevented bandit parties from being created one by one during each town visit after defeating the first bandit party during the Escort Merchant Caravan quest.
Fixed a misleading tooltip shown when trying to present a Dragon Banner to a kingdom leader.
Fixed a bug that caused troops given to the player temporarily for a quest to stay permanently.
Crafting
Increased the cut and pierce damage values of Decorated Warsword Blade, Decorated Short Warsword Blade and Decorated Long Warsword Blade crafting pieces.
Reduced the cut and pierce damage values of Bent Razor Head and Exceptional Eastern Glaive crafting pieces.
Audio
Fixed a bug that caused campaign sounds to persist after certain actions, like pressing ESC and continuing.

OnDeploymentFinished is now a mission object and mission behavior callback that is called for all mission types after the initial troop spawn.

If you have a custom deployment mission controller behavior (which you add to the Mission as a behavior) and which extends from the DeploymentMissionController abstract class, then you need to call Mission.OnDeploymentFinished(); when you finish spawning the initial troops and when the deployment phase is completed.

If you don't have a deployment mission controller behavior and if you just have a custom mission controller (which controls the mission flow), then you need to call Mission.OnInitialSpawnCompleted(BattleSide) during or after mission loading is finished. It could be in "AfterMissionLoadingFinished()" or within "OnMissionTick()".

Both pathways notify the mission that all initial troops and deployable entities are spawned. So the mission sends notification messages to all mission objects and behaviors to initialize themselves accordingly.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/26623866/fa7c7597c068ef8cd9611c32e18698e2696d158d.png"]
Greetings Warriors of Calradia!
We’re thrilled to announce the official release of War Sails - the naval expansion for Mount & Blade II: Bannerlord! It’s available now on PC and Consoles (PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S).
[dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/2927200/Mount__Blade_II_Bannerlord__War_Sails/"]
Join us in watching the War Sails Launch Trailer!

With War Sails, we’re bringing full naval warfare to Bannerlord for the first time. You’ll be able to command your own ships, lead fleets across the seas, and take part in large-scale naval battles as part of your campaign.
War Sails is a single-player expansion that plugs directly into the base game: new region & faction, new naval battles, and a lot of ways to get into trouble on the water.
The Nords & the Northern Kingdom
War Sails adds a new Viking-inspired faction: the Nords, based in the northern region.

You’ll travel through jagged coasts, taiga forests, and frozen fjords, visiting scattered settlements that feel almost like ships rising from the sea. There, you can trade, recruit warriors, work with Nord clans, or try to challenge their power yourself.
[img src="https://cdn.taleworlds.com/upload/news/NordsWSreleaseann.avif"]The Nords
Naval Battles
We’ve built a naval system inspired by historical medieval sea battles. You’ll command ships that are affected by wind and waves, decide when to ram, when to board, and when to keep your distance.

You can seize opportunities by boarding already engaged ships, prepare for an incoming attack by creating a floating fortress, or take a risk to tie down several enemies at once - giving your allies an edge elsewhere. You may also ram an enemy ship to sink it - or at least throw men off board, shatter oars, and compromise buoyancy.
Well-placed arrows and ballista fire can also ignite and destroy enemy sails and ships, forcing crews to abandon their stations.
[img src="https://cdn.taleworlds.com/upload/news/BallistaFireWSRelease.avif"]Burning Sails And Ships
A Larger World to Sail
Calradia now extends to the north, including a settled island, coastal routes, and open sea.
Weather plays a bigger role at sea: storms and currents can speed you up or grind you down. Riding the wind can make journeys faster, but attrition will punish long, poorly prepared expeditions.

Naval trade, piracy, and the Nord presence all feed back into the campaign. New trade goods, ship production, and coastal routes give certain towns a chance to grow rich - if they can survive raids and naval invasions.
Sieges can also involve the sea now: to fully cut off a coastal settlement, you’ll need a fleet to blockade it and stop supplies and reinforcements from slipping through.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/26623866/594d87663b64bec79eb1ba3210db06dabde7313a.png"]New Northern Region And Island
Building and Growing Your Fleet
War Sails adds 20 ships: 15 warships, 4 trade ships, and a civilian fishing vessel, all based on historical designs with their own handling and roles.
Equip ships with siege engines, cargo holds, upgraded sails, rams, and more
Capture enemy ships and figureheads in battle
Acquire vessels from shipyards that build and stock ships based on their town’s culture and development
[img src="https://cdn.taleworlds.com/upload/news/RamFireWSrelease.avif"]Ramming
Custom Naval Battles

If you just want to jump straight into fighting, you can set up custom naval battles. Pick your hero, factions, fleet compositions, ships (with randomized upgrades), crew setups, and then choose the wind, season, and time of day on River, Coastal, or Open Sea maps – no campaign required.
New Skills, Items & Troops

We’ve expanded the character system with Nord-themed hairstyles, beards, and tattoos, as well as three new nautical skills focused on navigation, tactics, and stewardship at sea. There are also new weapons and gear – spears, swords, axes, shields, and armor – along with mariner troop branches that perform better in naval combat. You’ll also meet new companions with seafaring backgrounds.
[img src="https://cdn.taleworlds.com/upload/news/NavalBattleWSrelease.avif"]Naval Battle
Getting Started: War Sails Questline

If you’d like a guided introduction, there’s a new questline that takes you from your first steps on deck to commanding a small fleet. Through cinematics, scripted missions, and familiar Mount & Blade gameplay, you’ll learn the basics of ship control, then take the fight to a pirate confederacy alongside your newfound allies.
Audio & Music
We’ve added new Mediterranean and Nordic-inspired tracks and updated the soundscape for life at sea: winds, waves, creaking hulls, and the chaos of boarding actions and ship-to-ship combat.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/26623866/d60fb07b521fabfe89b5f88ea0a1dde4c5dc9b9b.png"]

Alongside War Sails, we’re also bringing the base game Patch v1.3.4 to all players and platforms. Some of you have already played the patch during our Beta phase and provided immensely valuable feedback. This allowed us to further balance and refine the experience for which we’re truly grateful.
Here are the major highlights you’ll find in v1.3.4…
Alliances & Trade Agreements

Common enemies bring kingdoms closer to forming alliances, which encourages them to stand together against each other’s foes, while trade agreements incentivize caravan traffic between partner kingdoms.
Reworked War, Peace & Tribute Decision Scoring
Each conflict is now evaluated through a refined war progress score, resulting in more logical declarations and outcomes, while reducing the number of short wars.
Stealth & Disguise

Stealth and Disguise mechanics now power prison breaks, new hideout scenes, and hostile town infiltrations. Guards react to light, sound, and movement while you sneak, create distractions, eliminate targets quietly, and hide bodies. Disguise lets you scout and operate in hostile towns, though suspicious actions will quickly raise an alarm.
[img src="https://cdn.taleworlds.com/upload/news/StealthWSreleaseAnn.avif"]Stealth Kill
Fast Mode

Fast Mode is a new optional module that can be selected from the launcher on PC. It speeds up the passage of time: years are shorter, characters age faster, while skill progression and population turnover are tuned to match, making multi-generation dynasties and succession easier to experience in a single playthrough.

Deserters & Patrol Parties War now has additional consequences. After battles, fleeing survivors may regroup into tougher roaming bands, especially in war-torn regions. Towns can counter this by building Guard Houses, which produce patrol parties that protect villages, fight bandits, and assist nearby battles.
Random Events
These short moments of decision break up long journeys with brief and immersive stories that affect your traits, skills, party, items, or gold.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/26623866/0d2872e59bdbc48c02f1faf916e244ac1c6c2d74.png"]Random Events
Parley with Enemy
This feature lets you start conversations with nobles inside enemy settlements from a safe distance, without immediately risking a full battle.
Movement Control over Caravans
Through dialogue, you can change a caravan’s home town and instruct it to avoid specific kingdoms. Caravans were also adjusted to focus on maximizing trade amounts, value, and profits.
Reworked Army & Party AI

Armies and parties now keep a closer eye on their strength, wounded troops, and food when choosing targets or deciding whether to press on, pull back, or disband, which cuts down on detrimental marches and makes their actions more calculated.
Reworked Settlement Projects
We reworked settlement projects to balance impactful and situational projects, while introducing new options that give the player finer control over how they develop and manage their fief.
Recruiting Notables as Supporters

You can now recruit notables as supporters via dialogue. With enough relation and a one-time payment, they’ll back your clan, generating daily influence and shifting loyalty in your favor, but if relations drop too low, they can withdraw that support.
New Weapon – Slings
We also expanded the arsenal. Slings offer a fast ranged option with multiple ammo types, giving both you and certain troops a new way to pressure enemies at range.
[img src="https://cdn.taleworlds.com/upload/news/SlingShotWSreleaseAnn.avif"]Sling
Post-Knockout Troop Takeover
You can now take direct control of another troop after getting knocked out in battles and sieges. Less spectating, more raiding!
Crouched Ranged Attacks & Reloading

You can fire and reload while crouching with short bows, light crossbows, throwing knives, and throwing rocks, letting you stay low behind cover or move more naturally during both stealth missions and regular battles.
Overhauled Spear Bracing

Spearmen will now fight with their spears more often, switching to swords when close combat makes it the better choice. Spear bracing has been reworked with smoother animations and improved aiming. AI also targets the riders more accurately while bracing, making properly timed spear walls far better at stopping cavalry that tries to push through.
[img src="https://cdn.taleworlds.com/upload/news/SpearBracingWSreleaseAnn.avif"]Spear Bracing
Improved Melee, Ranged & Cavalry AI

Melee, ranged, and cavalry AI troops received improvements to targeting and movement. Cavalry charges and tracks targets in a more refined way, horse archers move with less zig-zagging and stay with their formations more. Melee troops now aim better and don’t shy away from mounted enemies. Ranged units lead projectiles at moving targets more effectively, better avoid friendly fire, and hold position once they are in good range.
New Main Menu Videos, Armour Pieces, Weapons, Shields, Scabbards & Holsters

New main menu videos were introduced for each culture, and several new armour pieces and equipment sets were added, including items that support stealth gameplay. Sturgia in particular received new shields and cultural bonuses, while newly added scabbards and holsters polish the overall look of troops.
[img src="https://cdn.taleworlds.com/upload/news/MainMenuVideosWSreleaseAnn.avif"]Main Menu Videos
Overhauled Mission Atmospheres

We fine-tuned atmosphere visuals with updated lighting and improved skybox textures. Towns, castles, and other scenes now have a greater range of custom environments tailored to cover specific times of day, together with improved global illumination.
New Music & Sounds
To further improve the immersion, we introduced new music and ambient sounds to support stealth missions, as well as broader audio additions.
Import/Export Hero Cheats
If you like to tweak your campaigns, new Import and Export options let you edit hero equipment, skills, attributes, gold, and appearance through save files and bring those changes back into the game.
Expanded Modding Capabilities

We expanded modding support with a wide range of new options. We added FMOD audio event support, made atmospheres and campaign time moddable, and introduced new ways to influence AI and mission behaviour through agent and weapon settings. We also added better support for custom world maps and a new XML Editor. Many of these improvements were inspired by feedback from our modding community.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/26623866/3bbd3a23c957d553c8e42e41741090bcf9ca1557.png"]XML Editor

Whether you’re diving into the v1.3.4 update or setting sail with War Sails, we truly hope you enjoy what we’ve been building. Your support, your feedback, and your passion continue to shape this game. Thank you for being part of this journey with us.
You can read the full v1.3.4 Patch Notes here.

Greetings Warriors of Calradia!
The v1.3.0 base game update is now available in Public Beta.

This update brings a wide range of improvements across the game, from new features to refined gameplay systems and technical upgrades - all aimed at making your time in Calradia more engaging and rewarding.

notes.title: Because this is a Beta, please note that

items.text: Save game compatibility is not guaranteed.
You may encounter instability, crashes, or unfinished elements as we continue development.
This phase aims to stress-test the update at scale, gather performance data, and make sure everything is solid when v1.3 launches in full.

If you’d prefer to wait for the most polished version, stick to the Live branch and jump into v1.3 with the launch of War Sails. But if you’d like to be part of the journey, opt into the Beta branch via the Steam Betas system today and tell us what’s working - and what still needs work.
Before jumping into the full patch notes, here's a quick recap of the many features being introduced.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/26623866/d1e911334c52d288d4c1c30e55cb406413c85117.png"]
Art
Changes
Added a new main menu video for each culture - 6 in total.
Added 4 new armor pieces: Blackened Boots, Blackened Armor, Blackened Cape, and Blackened Hood. These have a high stealth factor.
Added 4 new shields: Sturgian - Druzhinnik Kite Shield, Reinforced Leaf-Point Kite Shield, Leaf-Point Kite Shield; and Vlandian - Angular Kite Shield.
Added 6 new sword scabbards for existing blades.
Scene Atmospheres
We moved away from an automated interpolation of atmospheres based on time of day and instead introduced a greater range of custom environments that are tailored to cover specific times.
We further fine-tuned atmosphere values in general and improved our skybox textures.
Added and improved existing global illumination for various towns, castles, and keeps.

Campaign Map

Audio

Fixed a bug that caused some combat music to have the wrong transitions and mood jumps.

Fixed a bug that caused the wrong voice to be assigned to the character on the Character Creation screen.
UI
Changes
Implemented a new heir selection popup. The new popup presents information in a clearer, more visual format similar to the marriage popup, and shows the player’s relation to each candidate.
Pressing outside the Reserve popup now cancels instead of confirming.
Fixed a bug that caused the “Add to queue/Remove from queue” button to always display as “+”.

You can now reorder items on the right‑side queue via drag‑and‑drop, or click to manage an item directly.

Added additional warning menus for “Force Recruit” and “Force Goods” hostile actions to indicate that the action may cause war.

In a hero's encyclopedia page, the friends/enemies lists have been shortened to 3 rows, and the overflow is now displayed via a tooltip.

Made several improvements to the “Upgrade Troops” popup regarding horse requirements.
Disabled saves are now also selectable in the “Saved Campaigns” screen (they cannot be loaded).

In Custom Battle, the Siege Engine selection popup can now be exited without making a selection.

Fixes

Edited the layout of certain screens and adjusted the orientation of some non-Latin alphabets to resolve alignment issues.

Fixed a bug that allowed kingdom decisions to be viewed when they should be disabled.

Fixed a bug that prevented the “Charge to the Gate” order icon from appearing during sieges.
